report.headline: Desert Southwest heat may sap energy and sleep
report.quick_read: The main story is heat and humidity in the Desert Southwest, where some people may feel more fatigued, sleep may feel off, and effort may feel harder. Space weather is quiet. Ground sensors picked up an active, organized pattern, and today’s atmospheric background tones were measured clearly.

regional_watch.selection_method: At least two fixed anchors must support the same driver.
regional_watch.copy: Desert Southwest US — Heat and humidity stand out today. Some people may notice more fatigue, sleep feeling off, and lower exercise tolerance. This read is supported by conditions in Phoenix and Las Vegas.

space_watch.copy: Space weather is quiet. The day’s small peak and current levels line up: Kp is about 1.3 now, with solar wind near 260 km/s and light density. No Earth‑directed solar eruptions are indicated by today’s catalogs alone.

earth_signal.health_language: Possible effects may use 'may', 'can', or 'some people notice' without an appended disclaimer.
earth_signal.copy: Natural atmospheric background tones, often called Schumann frequencies, were measured around 7.43, 14.51, 21.99, 28.93, and 35.85 Hz. Ground sensors detected an active, organized pattern across the measured bands.

major_events.selection_method: Fresh yellow-or-higher GDACS/USGS events, deduplicated and capped.

platform_copy.facebook:
Feeling drained or sleeping a bit off? Heat and humidity are the top story today in parts of the Desert Southwest, and that combo can make effort feel harder.

Regional Watch
• Desert Southwest US: Heat and humidity may be part of what some people notice today—more fatigue, sleep feeling off, and lower exercise tolerance. This read is supported by conditions in Phoenix and Las Vegas.

Space Watch
Space weather is quiet. In plain terms, near‑Earth space is calm. Today’s quiet matches the day’s small peak. The Kp index, a simple gauge of geomagnetic activity, is around 1.3 now, and solar wind speed is near 260 km/s with a light density. These are calm conditions for most people.

Earth Signal
We also look at natural atmospheric background tones that hum along at set pitches; researchers call these Schumann frequencies. Today’s measured tones were about 7.43, 14.51, 21.99, 28.93, and 35.85 Hz. Ground sensors picked up an active, organized pattern across the measured bands.

Full report: gaiaeyes.com
Personalized patterns: gaiaeyes.com/app
